boot.evidence: Rust supervisor (forkpty + execv, PTY console drain, reap policy) booted the real guest: kernel 7.2.0-rc4-opt #1 SMP aarch64, guest CPUCOUNT 4 (seccomp SMP path), markers RUSTDAEMON_GUEST_START..RUSTDAEMON_DONE, guest powered itself off -> phase=completed detail=exit=0, no restart, 0 leftover processes of its own.

rust_daemon_protocol_parity.evidence: ci/verify-daemon-parity.sh runs the C daemon and the Rust daemon in turn on the same runtime with the same client and diffs normalised replies: 6/6 lines identical (status, ports, exec, expose, state file, HTTP /status body). Exit code 3 when the socket is unreachable, as in C.

cow_writer_byte_exact.evidence: rust/src/cow.rs vs write_cow_header_file(): same 3 MiB image -> cmp identical, sha256 01b716b4d10f60c751ce0b65ef46039c94c05b79ef0e703d48b47895e4e0dee8, same sparse size (CI gate). Real boots: both daemons wrote byte-identical COW files, sha256 052c0be926c24af44c6a0418843a36c5253abb5e40900ff76b6a20963123f2f9.

cow_isolation_verified_with_private_back.evidence: CORRECTED RESULT (see ubd_lock_contention below: the first boots of this session were silently DISKLESS, so they proved nothing about COW). Re-run against a private backing image (workspace/uml-forensics/cap7/debian-docker.ext4, sha256 7e1127d18ed826aa8e76d6cd8e7808b4997fa59f89832d9630e2e6971a3334c6): init reported 'root_mounted /dev/ubda -> /newroot' and 'SWITCH_ROOT_NOW', the guest wrote /root/rustboot.marker, the COW bitmap recorded 760 sectors and allocated 592 KB, and the backing image was byte-identical AND mtime-identical before/after (7e1127d1..., mtime 1793107661).

ubd_lock_contention.evidence: UML takes an exclusive host lock (F_SETLK) on the BACKING IMAGE. With the runit service's guest alive on the same image, every other boot fails: 'F_SETLK failed, file already locked by pid N', 'Failed to lock <image>, err = 11', 'Failed to initialize ubd device 0'. The guest then silently CONTINUES without a disk (its initramfs init prints NO_DISK and runs the entry script in RAM), so a docker run would appear to work while nothing persists. Reproduced with BOTH the C daemon (bin/uml4termuxd, v0.5.0 release) and the Rust daemon: the fault is in the environment/kernel behaviour, not in the port. Action taken: the Rust daemon gains a console scanner plus UML4TERMUXD_STRICT_UBD=1, which turns the failure into state=failed detail=ubd-attach and aborts instead of continuing diskless (verified on device: guard fired, guest script never ran, 0 leftovers).

rust_build_native_target.evidence: rustc host triple on Termux is aarch64-linux-android, so the device build IS the bionic target build: cargo test --release 33/33, clippy -D warnings clean, binary 1.6 MB (LTO + strip).

soak_real_disk_8_cycles.evidence: 8/8 cycles of the Rust daemon against a PRIVATE backing image with UML4TERMUXD_STRICT_UBD=1: every cycle reported disk=1 (init 'root_mounted /dev/ubda') switch_root=1 nodisk=0, 5 guest markers, phase=completed detail=exit=0, COW bitmap 752-776 sectors / 588-604 KB allocated, guest RSS 55-62 MB, 2-4 s per cycle, and the private image stayed byte- AND mtime-identical (7e1127d1..., mtime 1793107661) after all eight boots.

gvproxy_exposure_end_to_end.evidence: Rust daemon spawned gvproxy itself (proot-wrapped; bess sock + gv.sock API present, daemon logged 'gvproxy up pid=26934'), booted the docker guest to WEB_UP_MARKER with the disk attached, then 'expose 18124 8123' returned {"exposed":"127.0.0.1:18124 -> 192.168.127.2:8123"}, wrote the registry entry, and the host fetched http://127.0.0.1:18124/ through the full path (phone -> gvproxy -> BESS -> guest -> docker DNAT -> container) receiving the demo body 'gvproxy-bess-ok'. 'ports' then listed the registry entry, COW recorded 11432 sectors of docker writes, the backing image stayed unchanged, and after stop the daemon's gvproxy (pid 26934) was gone (kill(-pgid) group teardown) with no Rust daemon left behind.

gvproxy_port_collision.evidence: gvproxy hard-binds host 127.0.0.1:2222 for its SSH port forwarder, so a second gvproxy instance on the same device dies with 'cannot create ports forwarder: listen tcp 127.0.0.1:2222: bind: address already in use' (the runit service's gvproxy already held it; first e2e attempt). Fix shipped in the Rust daemon: gvproxy argv is now built by a tested helper that always passes -ssh-port, overridable per instance with UML4TERMUXD_GVPROXY_SSH_PORT (default 2222 keeps parity with the C daemon). The C daemon has no such override -- same limit applies to it.

notes: Phase-2 device evidence for the Rust daemon. CORRECTION: the first boot runs in this record were silently diskless -- UML could not attach ubd because another guest held the backing image's exclusive F_SETLK -- so they proved the supervisor path but NOT the disk/COW path. A re-run with a private backing image does prove it: ubda attaches, switch_root happens, 760 COW sectors record the guest's writes, and the image stays byte- and mtime-identical. The contention itself is now an explicit, reproducible finding with a guard in the Rust daemon (UML4TERMUXD_STRICT_UBD=1). Still open: gvproxy/exposure-registry with a live gvproxy attached to a real guest, a soak with the disk attached, and the C binary is still what ships in release v0.5.0. A corrected 8-cycle soak against a private image (STRICT_UBD on) now covers the disk path: 8/8 ok with root_mounted + switch_root, COW writes recorded, image byte/mtime-identical, 2-4 s per cycle.
known_limits_observed: one UML guest per backing image: UML holds an exclusive F_SETLK on it, so a second boot silently degrades to a diskless guest unless the daemon is run with UML4TERMUXD_STRICT_UBD=1
the runit service (legacy shell flow) may be holding that lock and may also rewrite the backing image (persistent, non-COW), so digest-sensitive runs must stop it first
gvproxy not attached during the boot tests, so inbound exposure is unverified in the Rust daemon
one gvproxy per host port 2222: set UML4TERMUXD_GVPROXY_SSH_PORT per instance (Rust daemon) or stop the other instance
